parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both services handle loans, so the module has one subject, but the two files reach persistence in different ways. LendingService.ts only uses the gateway ports: BookGateway, MemberGateway and LoanGateway. It turns the records they return into domain models (Book, Member, Loan). LoanHistoryService.ts skips that gateway layer. It injects PrismaService and calls the ORM client directly (db.loanEvent.create and db.loanEvent.findMany), mapping the raw rows by hand. Loan events belong with loans, and LoanGateway already serves as the loan port. Calling the ORM directly therefore goes around the module's own repository/port abstraction, which is a fail under the rubric. Both candidate flags (lines 16 and 20) match the source. One smaller point, not counted as a separate violation: both services generate IDs with their own in-memory counter ('loan-' + sequence and 'evt-' + counter). That is the same ad-hoc pattern written twice rather than one shared definition.

violations.message: LoanHistoryService injects PrismaService and calls db.loanEvent.create and db.loanEvent.findMany directly. This goes around the gateway/port abstraction (LoanGateway and its sibling gateways) that the rest of the module uses for persistence.
